atoms.title: The Importance of Bumblebees and Their Future

atoms.text: Bumblebees are important insects because they help pollinate crops and plants. However, since the late 1990s, bumblebee populations have declined by over 70% in the UK alone. Although bumblebees don’t make honey like honeybees, they still play an essential part in nature.
atoms.sound: Bumblebees are important insects because they help pollinate crops and plants. However, since the late 1990s, bumblebee populations have declined by over 70% in the UK alone. Although bumblebees don’t make honey like honeybees, they still play an essential part in nature.

atoms.text: A lot of bumblebees are dying because they are losing their homes. Contrary to popular belief, bumblebees do not have the typical honeybee hive. Most of the more common species prefer dry and dark holes. Their nests can turn up in different unexpected places: like in the ground or tucked away in a corner. Bumblebees generally like to stay as close to their hive as possible. Due to loss of nature, areas for bumblebees to comfortably nest in and to find enough food sources in are becoming fewer and fewer.

Most of the more common species prefer dry and dark holes. Their nests can turn up in different unexpected places: like in the ground or tucked away in a corner. Bumblebees generally like to stay as close to their hive as possible. Due to loss of nature, areas for bumblebees to comfortably nest in and to find enough food sources in are becoming less and less.

atoms.text: Apart from that, many bumblebees have been wiped out by pesticides. One type of pesticide responsible for this wipe-out are “neonics”. Studies show that this type of pesticide is especially poisonous for bumblebees, since it weakens the bees’ immune systems and negatively affects the bees’ different sense organs.

hint.text: Pesticides are used to keep bugs away from plants. Sadly, they can kill off a lot of important insects.
hint.label: Pesticides

atoms.text: Bumblebees play an important role in nature for a number of reasons. They not only pollinate many plants, but they are also a food source for different types of animals, such as birds and reptiles. Bumblebees should be protected at all costs. Making sure they don’t lose their homes and reducing pesticides will help to prevent any further damage to their population.

b: ++ Bumblebees play an important part in nature.
Declining bumblebee populations have an impact worldwide.

atoms.a: What is the author’s main reason for writing this text?
b: ++ To show how important bumblebees are and why bumblebees’ numbers are dropping.
To show how poisonous pesticides are.
To look at the impact declining insect populations have worldwide.

atoms.a: What evidence does the author state to support their claim?
b: ++ Bumblebees are declining because of habitat loss and use of pesticides.
Bumblebees live in different types of hives and enjoy pesticides.
Bumblebees are an important food source.

atoms.a: What specific evidence does the author use in the paragraph about using pesticides?
b: ++Neonic pesticides affect bees by weakening their immune systems and impacting their sense organs.
Studies show that neonic pesticides aren’t that bad.
A large portion of bumblebees are still living.
